currentContext.business: The Company manufactures, markets and distributes a wide-ranging portfolio of home and kitchen products and solutions, spanning pressure cookers, cookware and gas stoves that it makes itself, alongside kitchen appliances, spares and kitchen accessories that it markets and distributes. It reaches Indian households through a large network of value chain partners including dealers, authorised re-distributors, Prestige Xclusive stores, large format and modern-format retail, e-commerce platforms and the Canteen Stores Department. It also operates overseas through its UK subsidiary structure and a 51% owned modular-kitchen solutions business in India.

Brands / formats: Ultrafresh Modular Solutions (51% subsidiary, modular kitchens)

currentContext.strengths: Leadership position maintained in all key categories - pressure cookers, cookware, value added gas stoves, induction cooktops and kettles - with market share improvement in most of these categories during the year|Household brand with over seven decades of presence in India|Strong and well-balanced presence across all distribution channels, both online and offline, with collaborative channel-partner relationships; sales growth in FY 2025-26 was seen across categories and all key channels, breaking the low-growth phase of the previous few years|Innovation engine: new product introductions across cookers, cast iron and triply cookware, kitchen hoods, gas stoves, induction/radiant combo cooktops, hobs, mixer grinders and air fryers constituted more than 30% of sales|Go-To-Market (GTM) initiatives introduced during the year enabled sustained and consistent growth across all quarters, reinforcing market position|Governance standing: ESG rating of 68/100 ("Aspiring") for FY 2025 from NSE Sustainability Ratings and Analytics, with a Governance pillar score of 76 driven by board independence, regulatory compliance and committee structure; 11-member Board with a majority of non-executive independent directors|Part of the TTK Group, an industrial house with a nine-decade reputation for ethical practices and governance
currentContext.strategies: Defend and extend leadership in core kitchenware categories (Pressure Cookers, Cookware, value-added Gas Stoves, Induction Cooktops, Kettles), where market share improved in most categories during the year.|Drive growth through continuous new-product introduction across categories - Cooker, cast iron and light-weight cast iron cookware, Safesense Kitchen Hood, Triply Cookware range, Gas Stoves, Induction-Radiant Heater Combo Cooktops, Hobs, Mixer Grinders, Air Fryers and other small domestic appliances - with new introductions already contributing over 30% of sales.|Indigenise manufacturing in India for new and innovative products currently imported from China (indigenisation described as 'undergoing').|Run innovative 'Go-To-Market' (GTM) strategies designed to deliver sustained, consistent growth across all quarters and across channels and categories.|Maintain a strong, well-balanced omni-channel presence - general trade, Prestige Xclusives, modern format stores and e-commerce - nurturing channel-partner relationships and closing distribution gaps through seamless integration of traditional and modern trade.|Manage channel conflict without diluting product value or resorting to aggressive, unsustainable pricing.|Scale 'Judge' as a tactical brand following its FY2023-24 repositioning; it grew 59% to roughly Rs 108 crores of sales.|The Company's stated philosophy is to follow fair business and organizational practices to fulfil its mission of Quality Consumer Products at affordable prices and, in the process, deliver long-term sustainable shareholder value; governance is described as aiming to enhance stakeholder value sustainably and to travel beyond statutory requirements to encompass social responsibilities. Consistent with this, dividend is declared annually by shareholders as ordinary business at the AGM on the Re 1 face-value equity shares, alongside adoption of the audited standalone and consolidated financial statements. Capital deployed in group entities is held through a 100% overseas holding subsidiary structure (TTK British Holdings / Horwood Homewares) and a 51% domestic stake in Ultrafresh Modular Solutions, with funding support to subsidiaries extended in the form of inter-corporate deposits carrying interest. CSR is applicable to the Company under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 and sustainability is stated to be integral to strategy, with the conviction that business performance and sustainability must travel in tandem.|Occupational Health & Safety management system implemented across operations and aligned to ISO 45001; all production units are certified by independent third parties to ISO 45001:2018 and undergo periodic external audits.|100% of plants and offices assessed during the year on both Working Conditions and Health & Safety, by the entity, statutory authorities or third parties.|Worker LTIFR (per million person-hours) improved to 0.34 in 2025-26 from 0.64 in 2024-25, with nil fatalities and nil high-consequence injuries reported for employees and workers.|Structured hazard-identification framework — HIRA and JSA for routine work; permit-to-work, management-of-change and pre-start-up safety reviews for non-routine work such as maintenance, shutdowns and new projects.|Digital safety-alert platform for real-time reporting of unsafe acts, unsafe conditions and near misses, backed by the 'Right to Stop Work' principle (one of the 7 Safety Fundamentals) allowing employees and contract workers to halt unsafe work without fear of reprisal.|CAPA discipline: all incidents and near misses investigated via root-cause (Why-Why) analysis, with time-bound owner-assigned actions tracked to closure and engineering controls such as machine guarding, safety interlocks and automation of high-risk operations.|Diversity: the Company is in the process of inducting more female workers on the shop floor and expects this proportion to rise in coming years, alongside multi-skilling of the workforce.|Value-chain governance: a Code of Conduct for Value Chain Partners requiring safe workplaces and OHS compliance, with checklist-based assessment at induction repeated annually, a self-assessment questionnaire during the year, and remedial guidance for low-scoring partners; no significant health, safety or working-condition concern was reported.|ESG considerations are integrated into the enterprise risk-management process in line with regulatory requirements, with a SEBI (LODR)-mandated Risk Management Committee, a board-approved Risk Management Policy published on the Company website, and periodic risk audits by independent professional firms.|Employee healthcare access via occupational health centres, a 24x7 helpline, annual health checks, ESI and third-party medical insurance tie-ups; life insurance / compensatory cover in the event of death is extended to workers (not to employees), and no transition-assistance programme is provided.
currentContext.expansion: The routed sections carry no conventional capacity-expansion or greenfield-plant narrative; TTK Prestige's disclosed capital deployment in FY2025-26 sits in manufacturing footprint upgrades, sustainability infrastructure and R&D build-out across its named plants at Hosur, Coimbatore, Khardi, Karjan and Roorkee. On the R&D side, the company set up a New Innovation Centre for Appliances in Bengaluru during the year, while the upgrade of its Kitchenware R&D Centre at Hosur is stated to be in progress. On the process/technology side, the company implemented raw material blanking line automation at the Hosur and Karjan plants, developed indigenously with no imported technology, citing safety, consistent quality, continuous production and higher productivity as benefits; new technological equipment for cookware lines was installed at the Karjan plant, explicitly for safety improvement, quality enhancement and capacity enhancement. The largest identifiable physical asset addition is rooftop solar: a 600 KW rooftop solar plant at Coimbatore, a 3000 KW rooftop solar plant at Karjan (combined with third-party hybrid green power to take green power capacity to 79 Lakh Kwh/year), a 2000 KW rooftop solar plant at Khardi installed in March 2026, and an 850 KW rooftop solar plant at Roorkee also installed in March 2026 — the Khardi and Roorkee installations being explicitly forward-dated, with their CO2 reduction benefits stated to accrue from FY27 onwards. The company also reports capital expenditure on fire risk mitigation, security risk mitigation, heat recovery exchangers, energy-efficient motors, fans and lighting, variable frequency drives on significant energy-consuming machines, air compressor process optimisation, water conservation and rainwater harvesting. No plant capacity figures, utilisation levels, commissioning schedules for new manufacturing lines, acquisitions or new geographies are disclosed in the routed text.
currentContext.mdna: Kitchenware and kitchen-appliances demand is resilient and largely domestic, supported by urbanisation, replacement demand, rising incomes, organised retail expansion and adoption of modular kitchens.|Consumer preference is shifting toward convenient, energy-efficient and premium products, with premiumisation visible in urban markets while affordability/value remains important in price-sensitive mass segments.|Health, safety, ease of use, energy efficiency, brand trust and after-sales service have become key purchase factors; promotional offers and digital marketing significantly influence buying decisions.|Channel mix continues shifting to an omnichannel model - e-commerce and quick-commerce growing strongly, organised retail expanding in urban and semi-urban areas, while general trade and exclusive outlets remain key. Management states companies with strong brands and multichannel reach are better positioned to grow.|Growth in FY2025-26 was broad-based across categories and all key channels, breaking the low-growth phase of the last few years; general trade grew after a lag of about three years and the traditional channel (general trade, exclusive stores, e-commerce, modern trade) grew 11.6%.|Demand for non-gas appliances rose in the final quarter, driven by the Middle East conflicts.|Competition has intensified with multiple players, driving focus on pricing, innovation, branding and omni-channel distribution.|Moderate input-cost pressure persists, with late-year geopolitical tensions raising input and freight costs, though impacts were described as manageable through sourcing and pricing strategies.|Local manufacturing is gaining traction supported by policy initiatives, and sustainability considerations are growing in importance.|Exports were moderate, pressured by subdued global demand, higher freight costs and geopolitical uncertainty; late-year West Asia tensions raised logistics costs and affected timelines and margins, though diversified markets and cost management kept exports stable.|India's macro backdrop was resilient - growth supported by strong domestic consumption, sustained public capex and gradual improvement in private investment, with contained inflation supporting consumer confidence.

risks.risk: Highly fragmented kitchenware industry with a large unorganized/regional segment
risks.note: Lower-cost unorganized offerings exert continuous pricing pressure, particularly in rural and semi-urban markets, constraining the ability of organized players to expand market share and sustain premium positioning.

risks.risk: Limited pricing power — inability to fully pass on cost increases
risks.note: In a highly price-sensitive competitive market, management states the ability to fully pass cost increases to customers may remain constrained, which could adversely impact margins.

risks.risk: Input cost, energy and supply-chain inflation tied to geopolitics and trade policy
risks.note: Evolving macro conditions, the ongoing West Asia crisis, shifting global trade dynamics, inflation, currency volatility and raw-material/energy cost swings could raise input costs; any escalation in tensions or change in tariff structures may further impact sourcing costs and logistics.

risks.risk: Intensifying competition from organized players and new-age brands; innovation execution risk
risks.note: Management flags that continuous product innovation, premiumization and differentiation are critical for sustaining growth, and that any delay in launching new products or adapting to changing consumer preferences may affect performance.

risks.risk: Growth outlook contingent on the macro/GDP environment
risks.note: The Company links confidence in maintaining its growth path with stable operating margins to projected GDP growth of 6.2% being achieved; its medium-term growth and margin aspiration is explicitly stated as subject to macroeconomic, geopolitical and market conditions beyond its control.

risks.risk: Cybersecurity and information-security exposure from rising digital adoption and AI
risks.note: No material cybersecurity incident was reported during the year, but attempted intrusion events were identified and contained; the Company acknowledges heightened risk exposure and an expanding attack surface driven by digital adoption and advances in technologies such as artificial intelligence.

risks.risk: Foreign currency exposure from imports and exports, principally USD
risks.note: The Group imports raw materials and finished goods and makes export sales, leaving it exposed to INR movements chiefly against the US Dollar; exposure is managed by entering forward contracts against foreign currency vendor payables.

While the customer base is described as diversified with no customer above 10% of outstanding receivables at year-end, a small group of customers each owing more than 5% of total receivables accounted for a fifth of receivables outstanding, and the count of such customers rose year on year.

one-line thesis: TTK Prestige delivered a robust Q4FY26 with 14.4% domestic growth driven by tactical induction cooktop demand and general trade recovery, offsetting export supply chain constraints. While gross margins expanded due to mix and inventory benefits, management flagged inevitable margin pressure from ~10% input cost inflation and guided for continued heavy capex/opex investment (INR 200cr strategy + INR 300cr capex) over the next two years, temporarily suppressing EBITDA margins before targeting a return to 13-14%.
financial scorecard: Revenue: Q4 +12.5% (Domestic +14.4%, Exports constrained); FY26 +9.6%. EBITDA: Q4 INR 81.7cr (+43.8%); FY26 +12%. PAT: FY26 INR 185cr (+14%). Order Book: Not disclosed (Make-to-stock/retail driven). Net Debt: Not explicitly detailed; focus on funding INR 500cr total investment plan. One-offs: Exceptional expenses related to new Labour Code compliance; INR 200cr strategic transformation spend over 3 years (started Q4FY25).
guidance: Revenue Growth: Greedy for growth; no specific % given. Margin: Short-term dip expected due to investments; target return to 13-14% EBITDA in ~2 years. Order Inflow: Strong domestic demand; exports limited by supply chain. Capex/Commissioning: INR 300cr capex planned over next 2 years; Triply facility in Karjan recently expanded; utilization at 85% (kitchenware) and 75-80% (appliances).
order book & pipeline: N/A for retail model; Channel inventory reported as normalized with no Q3-to-Q4 GST-driven channel filling distortions.
segment / subsidiary detail: Appliances grew ~20% in Q4 (boosted by induction cooktop frenzy); Kitchenware grew ~10% FY26. Cookers shifting to 50-55% stainless steel mix. Induction cooktops seeing accelerated adoption due to global volatility/substitution. Cookware growth driven by Triply, Cast Iron, and Ceramic innovations (>20% industry growth in these sub-segments).
growth verticals / optionality: Exclusive 'Prestige' store expansion (700+ stores, added ~100 in Q4); Tier 2/3 penetration; 'Judge' brand for mass segment (operating independently); Quick commerce leadership; Product premiumization via new materials.
margins & cost dynamics: Input cost inflation ~10% average (up to 15% in specific commodities like Al, Steel, Copper) post-West Asia conflict. Q4 gross margin expansion driven by favorable product mix (high-margin appliances), internal inventory management, and cost reduction initiatives, not just price hikes. Price increases implemented mid-Q4 will impact Q1FY27 more significantly.
capex / expansion: Total ~INR 300cr planned over next 2 years. Recent expansion in Triply cookware facility at Karjan. Focus on in-sourcing kitchenware; hybrid model for appliances with exclusive partners. Investments in R&D, design centers, and automation.
capital allocation: INR 200cr strategic transformation spend over 3 years (people, processes, R&D, marketing); INR 300cr capex for capacity expansion. Advertising spend maintained at 5-6% of sales. No specific dividend/buyback commentary; focus on reinvestment for growth.
risks & watch-items: Sustained input cost inflation eroding margins if price hikes stall demand. Geopolitical tensions disrupting supply chains (impacted exports). Intense competition from new D2C players on pricing in low-end segments. Execution risk on INR 500cr investment plan delivering expected ROI.
management quality / tone: Cautiously Optimistic; Transparent on cost pressures; Aggressive on reinvestment ('greedy for growth'); Confident in long-term structural story despite short-term volatility.
non-obvious takeaways: Management explicitly separated the 'Judge' brand P&L trajectory as independent, suggesting a firewall against margin dilution in the mass segment. The 'frenzy' in induction cooktops is viewed as a tactical multi-quarter opportunity driven by global instability, not just seasonal demand. General Trade rebound is company-specific due to distribution hygiene, contrary to industry lag.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rising aluminum, steel, and copper prices (~10-15% inflation) squeezing industry margins. | TTK Prestige Ltd | beneficiary | High | Strong pricing power, favorable product mix shift to premium appliances, and prior inventory management allowed Q4 margin expansion despite inflation; well-positioned to pass on costs compared to unbranded competitors. |
| New D2C entrants competing aggressively on price in the low-end kitchenware segment. | Unbranded/Small Local Players | loser | Med | TTK's dual-brand strategy (Prestige for premium, Judge for mass) and focus on innovation/material upgrades (Triply, Ceramic) creates a moat that pure-play low-cost competitors cannot easily breach without sacrificing viability. |

themes.title: Consumer durables, cooling & electricals
themes.need: Rising incomes, electrification and a record cooling season drive consumer-electricals and appliances - HAVELLS/VOLTAS/BLUESTARCO/SYMPHONY/ORIENTELEC on cooling & electricals; TTKPRESTIG/STOVEKRAFT/BAJAJELEC/EUREKAFORB on kitchen/home; CROMPTON-tier fans & pumps; premiumization + GST 2.0 + summer demand expand the organized share. Q1FY27's small-cap read: SONAMLTD grew revenue 75.6% YoY to INR 66.57cr on a cheap raw-material inventory position taken 6-7 months in advance while selling prices rose - management explicitly called the 75% print non-repeatable and guided FY27 to 25-30% with a Q2 floor of INR 40-50cr - and is pivoting from volume to INR 5,000-15,000 value clocks with capacity utilisation still only 60-70%.
themes.driver: Summer cooling demand; GST 2.0 price cuts; festive restocking; commodity-cost tailwind on margins; premiumization/ASP mix shift.

hero.oneLiner: TTK Prestige is a seven-decade-old Indian home and kitchen appliances company whose Prestige brand holds leadership positions across pressure cookers, cookware, value-added gas stoves, induction cooktops and kettles.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: TTK Prestige is a seven-decade-old Indian home and kitchen appliances company whose Prestige brand holds leadership positions across pressure cookers, cookware, value-added gas stoves, induction cooktops and kettles.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures, markets and distributes a wide-ranging portfolio of home and kitchen products and solutions, spanning pressure cookers, cookware and gas stoves that it makes itself, alongside kitchen appliances, spares and kitchen accessories that it markets and distributes. It reaches Indian households through a large network of value chain partners including dealers, authorised re-distributors, Prestige Xclusive stores, large format and modern-format retail, e-commerce platforms and the Canteen Stores Department. It also operates overseas through its UK subsidiary structure and a 51% owned modular-kitchen solutions business in India.

- Ultrafresh Modular Solutions Limited, India (New Delhi) — subsidiary: 51% held by the Company; acquired 04/01/2023; modular kitchen solutions business; does not participate in the listed entity's Business Responsibility initiatives. Mr. Saranyan Rajagopalan is a director on its board

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Appliances grew ~20% in Q4 (boosted by induction cooktop frenzy); Kitchenware grew ~10% FY26. Cookers shifting to 50-55% stainless steel mix. Induction cooktops seeing accelerated adoption due to global volatility/substitution. Cookware growth driven by Triply, Cast Iron, and Ceramic innovations (>20% industry growth in these sub-segments).

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Cooking (manufactured):** Pressure Cookers, Cookware, Cast iron cookware, Light weight cast iron cookware, Triply Cookware, Gas Stoves
- **Kitchen Appliances (marketed/distributed):** Induction Cooktop, Induction - Radiant Heater Combo Cooktops, Mixer Grinders, Kettles, Air Fryers, Hobs, Safesense Kitchen Hood, Other small domestic appliances

- **Brands / formats:** Prestige, Prestige Xclusive stores, Horwood Homewares (UK step-down subsidiary), Ultrafresh Modular Solutions (51% subsidiary, modular kitchens)

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Indian domestic households - demand described as largely domestic, supported by replacement demand, rising incomes and urbanisation
- Kitchenware and Kitchen Appliances industry in India (pressure cookers, cookware, gas stoves, small appliances)
- Modular kitchens (through Ultrafresh Modular Solutions)
- Exports - modest, contributing 2.46% of turnover, described as impacted by subdued global demand and higher freight costs
- United Kingdom / overseas via TTK British Holdings and Horwood Homewares
- Channels: general trade, Prestige Xclusives, modern format stores, organised retail, e-commerce and …

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: N/A for retail model; Channel inventory reported as normalized with no Q3-to-Q4 GST-driven channel filling distortions.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: Greedy for growth; no specific % given. Margin: Short-term dip expected due to investments; target return to 13-14% EBITDA in ~2 years. Order Inflow: Strong domestic demand; exports limited by supply chain. Capex/Commissioning: INR 300cr capex planned over next 2 years; Triply facility in Karjan recently expanded; utilization at 85% (kitchenware) and 75-80% (appliances).

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Exclusive 'Prestige' store expansion (700+ stores, added ~100 in Q4); Tier 2/3 penetration; 'Judge' brand for mass segment (operating independently); Quick commerce leadership; Product premiumization via new materials.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Kitchenware and kitchen-appliances demand is resilient and largely domestic, supported by urbanisation, replacement demand, rising incomes, organised retail expansion and adoption of modular kitchens.
- Consumer preference is shifting toward convenient, energy-efficient and premium products, with premiumisation visible in urban markets while affordability/value remains important in price-sensitive mass segments.
- Health, safety, ease of use, energy efficiency, brand trust and after-sales service have become key purchase factors; promotional offers and digital marketing significantly influence buying decisions.
- Channel mix continues shifting to an omnichannel model - e-commerce and quick-commerce growing strongly, organised retail expanding in urban and semi-urban areas, while general trade and exclusive outlets remain key. Management states companies with strong brands and multichannel reach are better positioned to grow.
- Growth in FY2025-26 was broad-based across categories and all key channels, breaking the low-growth phase of the last few years; general trade grew after a lag of about three years and the traditional channel (general trade, exclusive stores, e-commerce, modern trade) grew 11.6%.
- Demand for non-gas appliances rose in the final quarter, driven by the Middle East conflicts.
- Competition has intensified with multiple players, driving focus on pricing, innovation, branding and omni-channel distribution.
- Moderate input-cost pressure persists, with late-year geopolitical tensions raising input and freight costs, though impacts were described as manageable through sourcing and pricing strategies.
- Local manufacturing is gaining traction supported by policy initiatives, and sustainability considerations are growing in importance.
- Exports were moderate, pressured by subdued global demand, higher freight costs and geopolitical uncertainty; late-year West Asia tensions raised logistics costs and affected timelines and margins, though diversified markets and cost management kept exports stable.
- India's macro backdrop was resilient - growth supported by strong domestic consumption, sustained public capex and gradual improvement in private investment, with contained inflation supporting consumer confidence.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Input cost inflation ~10% average (up to 15% in specific commodities like Al, Steel, Copper) post-West Asia conflict. Q4 gross margin expansion driven by favorable product mix (high-margin appliances), internal inventory management, and cost reduction initiatives, not just price hikes. Price increases implemented mid-Q4 will impact Q1FY27 more significantly.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: INR 200cr strategic transformation spend over 3 years (people, processes, R&D, marketing); INR 300cr capex for capacity expansion. Advertising spend maintained at 5-6% of sales. No specific dividend/buyback commentary; focus on reinvestment for growth.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The routed sections carry no conventional capacity-expansion or greenfield-plant narrative; TTK Prestige's disclosed capital deployment in FY2025-26 sits in manufacturing footprint upgrades, sustainability infrastructure and R&D build-out across its named plants at Hosur, Coimbatore, Khardi, Karjan and Roorkee. On the R&D side, the company set up a New Innovation Centre for Appliances in Bengaluru during the year, while the upgrade of its Kitchenware R&D Centre at Hosur is stated to be in progress. On the process/technology side, the company implemented raw material blanking line automation at the Hosur and Karjan plants, developed indigenously with no imported technology, citing safety, consistent quality, continuous production and higher productivity as benefits; new technological equipment for cookware lines was installed at the Karjan plant, explicitly for safety improvement, quality enhancement and capacity enhancement. The largest identifiable physical asset addition is rooftop solar: a 600 KW rooftop solar plant at Coimbatore, a 3000 KW rooftop solar plant at Karjan (combined with third-party hybrid green power to take green power capacity to 79 Lakh Kwh/year), a 2000 KW rooftop solar plant at Khardi installed in March 2026, and an 850 KW rooftop solar plant at Roorkee also installed in March 2026 — the Khardi and Roorkee installations being explicitly forward-dated, with their CO2 reduction benefits stated to accrue from FY27 onwards. The company also reports capital expenditure on fire risk mitigation, security risk mitigation, heat recovery exchangers, energy-efficient motors, fans and lighting, variable frequency drives on significant energy-consuming machines, air compressor process optimisation, water conservation and rainwater harvesting. No plant capacity figures, utilisation levels, commissioning schedules for new manufacturing lines, acquisitions or new geographies are disclosed in the routed text.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously Optimistic; Transparent on cost pressures; Aggressive on reinvestment ('greedy for growth'); Confident in long-term structural story despite short-term volatility.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Leadership position maintained in all key categories - pressure cookers, cookware, value added gas stoves, induction cooktops and kettles - with market share improvement in most of these categories during the year
- Household brand with over seven decades of presence in India
- Strong and well-balanced presence across all distribution channels, both online and offline, with collaborative channel-partner relationships; sales growth in FY 2025-26 was seen across categories and all key channels, breaking the low-growth phase of the previous few years
- Innovation engine: new product introductions across cookers, cast iron and triply cookware, kitchen hoods, gas stoves, induction/radiant combo cooktops, hobs, mixer grinders and air fryers constituted more than 30% of sales
- Go-To-Market (GTM) initiatives introduced during the year enabled sustained and consistent growth across all quarters, reinforcing market position
- Governance standing: ESG rating of 68/100 ("Aspiring") for FY 2025 from NSE Sustainability Ratings and Analytics, with a Governance pillar score of 76 driven by board independence, regulatory compliance and committee structure; 11-member Board with a majority of non-executive independent directors
- Part of the TTK Group, an industrial house with a nine-decade reputation for ethical practices and governance

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Sustained input cost inflation eroding margins if price hikes stall demand. Geopolitical tensions disrupting supply chains (impacted exports). Intense competition from new D2C players on pricing in low-end segments. Execution risk on INR 500cr investment plan delivering expected ROI.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Management explicitly separated the 'Judge' brand P&L trajectory as independent, suggesting a firewall against margin dilution in the mass segment. The 'frenzy' in induction cooktops is viewed as a tactical multi-quarter opportunity driven by global instability, not just seasonal demand. General Trade rebound is company-specific due to distribution hygiene, contrary to industry lag.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Defend and extend leadership in core kitchenware categories (Pressure Cookers, Cookware, value-added Gas Stoves, Induction Cooktops, Kettles), where market share improved in most categories during the year.
- Drive growth through continuous new-product introduction across categories - Cooker, cast iron and light-weight cast iron cookware, Safesense Kitchen Hood, Triply Cookware range, Gas Stoves, Induction-Radiant Heater Combo Cooktops, Hobs, Mixer Grinders, Air Fryers and other small domestic appliances - with new introductions already contributing over 30% of sales.
- Indigenise manufacturing …

challenges.body:

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rising aluminum, steel, and copper prices (~10-15% inflation) squeezing industry margins. | TTK Prestige Ltd | beneficiary | High | Strong pricing power, favorable product mix shift to premium appliances, and prior inventory management allowed Q4 margin expansion despite inflation; well-positioned to pass on costs compared to unbranded competitors. |
| New D2C entrants competing aggressively on price in the low-end kitchenware segment. | Unbranded/Small Local Players | loser | Med | TTK's dual-brand strategy (Prestige for premium, Judge for mass) and focus on innovation/material upgrades (Triply, Ceramic) creates a moat that pure-play low-cost competitors cannot easily breach without sacrificing viability. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Regulation - New Labour Code] "During FY25-26 the Company had assessed the incremental impact of Rs 16.94 Crores arising from the change in the definition of 'wages' under the New Labour Code", presented as an Exceptional item for the year ended March 31, 2026; after aligning salary structures to the Labour Codes, "the consequent reversal to the provision to the extent of Rs 7.3 Crores has been presented as an Exceptional Item" for the quarter ended June 30, 2026.
- [UK market outlook] Horwood's market is guided to "5-8% market CAGR over the decade driven by home-cooking, sustainability, and online retail trends", though near-term "growth is expected to remain modest, with Q2 wholesale volumes likely flat to slightly higher than expected" and "Political uncertainty remains elevated"; the UK showed inflation steady at 2.8% and Bank Rate unchanged at 3.75% in June 2026.
- [Macro watchpoints] Margin pressure came "from higher commodity and logistics costs, driven largely by disruptions associated with the Middle East crisis"; the Rupee "touched a record low of Rs 96.8/USD in May, before recovering to Rs 94-95/USD by quarter-end".
- [Current trading] "Encouraging demand trends witnessed in Q1 FY27 have largely continued in July 2026", with festive-season restocking expected to support the consumer categories.
